event.canonical_title: Kimmel Moves Talarico Interview to YouTube Amid FCC Threats
event.summary: Jimmy Kimmel announced that his interview with Texas Senate candidate James Talarico will not air on television due to alleged threats from the FCC against his show and the ABC network. Instead, the interview will be available on YouTube. Kimmel described the situation as 'unusual circumstances' surrounding the interview.

event_overview.title: About Kimmel Moves Talarico Interview to YouTube Amid FCC Threats
event_overview.subject: Kimmel Moves Talarico Interview to YouTube Amid FCC Threats
event_overview.summary: In September 2026, Jimmy Kimmel said an interview with Texas Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico would be released on the "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" YouTube channel rather than carried in the program’s ABC television broadcast. Kimmel described the decision as a response to what he said were FCC threats affecting the show, ABC, and local affiliates; the move highlighted how federal broadcast-election rules apply to licensed television stations but not to online distribution.

facts.label: Dates and release format
facts.value: Kimmel announced the change on September 9, 2026, and the interview was released online on September 10 rather than aired as part of the ABC broadcast.

facts.label: Participants
facts.value: The interview paired Jimmy Kimmel with James Talarico, who was reported as the Democratic candidate for Texas’s U.S. Senate seat and is also a sitting Texas House member representing District 50.

facts.label: News-program exception
facts.value: Section 315 excludes candidate appearances on bona fide newscasts, news interviews, qualifying documentaries, and on-the-spot news coverage from being treated as a candidate’s station “use”; FCC guidance has evaluated bona fide news interviews based on scheduling, producer control, and newsworthiness-based editorial judgment.

facts.label: Scope of the FCC rules at issue
facts.value: The statute addresses use of a “broadcasting station,” which is why the reported workaround used an online platform rather than the ABC broadcast feed; this does not itself resolve any dispute over the FCC’s authority or the applicability of an exemption to a particular program.

event_overview.scope_note: This timeline covers the September 2026 decision to distribute this specific Kimmel–Talarico interview online and the stated FCC-related rationale, not the full Texas Senate campaign, all prior ABC–FCC disputes, or a legal adjudication of the parties’ competing claims.
